name: LocaleAsset
src_typeComment: One language, as an asset: a locale code (the inherited `id` field — "en", "fr", "de", "en-PT"), a human-readable name for a language picker, and a flat key -> text table.  This is a GameDataAsset subclass on purpose: LocaleRegistry is a GameDataRegistry<LocaleAsset>, so looking a language up by its code is the registry's existing GetById() and nothing new had to be written for it. ONE ASSET PER LANGUAGE, not one per string — a per-string asset would mean thousands of .asset files and a merge conflict on every translation pass.

src_serialized.name: displayName
src_serialized.tooltip: Shown to the player in a language picker, in that language — "English", "Français", "Deutsch". The inherited Id above is the code the game uses internally.

src_serialized.name: systemLanguage
src_serialized.tooltip: Which Application.systemLanguage this locale serves. Set it and LocalizationManager can pick this language automatically on a player's first launch. Leave Unknown to opt out of auto-detection — the code is never guessed from the id, so a non-standard code like "en-PT" cannot be mis-detected.

src_serialized.name: fontOverride
src_serialized.tooltip: Optional. A font asset to swap in while this locale is active — the practical answer to a language whose glyphs the default font does not contain. LocalizedText applies it automatically.

src_serialized.name: entries
src_serialized.tooltip: The translation table. Normally filled in by the CSV/JSON importer (Toolkit > Localization Importer) rather than typed by hand.
